h1: Planning a brewpub crawl in an Indian city with safe transport
title: Planning a Safe Brewpub Crawl in India | Craft Beer School
desc: How to plan a brewpub crawl in an Indian city: how many stops, what to order, how to pace it and how to get everyone home safely.
teaser: Three brewpubs, four hours and a ride home booked before the first beer. That is a good crawl.
standfirst: Bengaluru, Pune, Gurugram and other Indian cities now have enough brewpubs close together for a proper crawl. Here is how to plan one that you enjoy and remember, with transport sorted before anyone orders.
sections:
The most important decision on a brewpub crawl is made before the first beer: how everyone gets home. Decide it in the group chat, not at 11 pm. The options are simple. Use ride-hailing cabs between stops. Use the metro where your city's line connects the brewpubs. Or have one person stay completely sober and drive, with everyone agreeing to that in advance.

Nobody drives after drinking. Not "just two pints". Indian roads at night are hard enough sober and drink-driving checks are common in big cities. Book cabs from inside the brewpub, wait indoors and share the trip details with a friend. Groups travelling late should stick together until everyone is dropped.

A crawl is not a race. Three brewpubs over about four hours gives you time to eat, talk and actually taste the beer. Pick brewpubs within a short cab ride of each other so you are not spending half the evening in traffic. In Bengaluru or Gurugram, that often means choosing one neighbourhood rather than crossing the city.

Book tables on weekends. Popular brewpubs fill up after 8 pm. Check closing times too. Last orders vary by state and city. Some areas close earlier than visitors expect. Check dry days for your date as well, since brewpubs cannot serve on them.

Most Indian brewpubs offer a tasting flight or small pours of their house beers. Order those at each stop. A flight of four to six small glasses lets you taste the whole range for about the alcohol of a pint or so. Pick one favourite to order as a full glass if you like.

Taste lightest to strongest: a wheat beer or lager first, then pale ales and IPAs, then stouts and strong beers. Our guide to beer with street food has ideas for matching the snacks you will order along the way.

Order food at each brewpub. Brewpub menus in India are built for beer, with fried snacks, kebabs, pizzas and small plates. Food slows the absorption of alcohol and makes the evening better. Spicy food changes how beer tastes too. Heat makes bitterness feel sharper, so a malty or wheat beer often suits a fiery dish better than a big IPA. Our guide to Indian food and beer pairing goes further.

Drink a glass of water with every beer. Ask for it on the table from the start. Most brewpubs will bring a jug without fuss.

Here is one shape that works on a Saturday in most big Indian cities:

  • 6 pm, first stop: arrive early while it is quiet. Order a flight and a couple of small plates. This is where you taste most carefully.
  • 7.30 pm, second stop: a short cab ride away. Order tasters again plus something more filling, since this is dinner.
  • 9 pm, third stop: one full glass of your favourite style, plenty of water and dessert if they do it.
  • 10.30 pm: cabs home, booked from inside.

Starting early matters more than people think. Brewpubs are calmer before 8 pm, the staff have time to talk about the beer and you finish before the late-night traffic and surge pricing. It also leaves Sunday morning for something other than recovering.

Keep a simple kitty for the group on a payment app. Splitting three bills at three stops is slow and tends to end with somebody ordering one more round to make the maths easier.
Know the rules where you are

The legal drinking age in India varies by state, from 18 in some states to 25 in others. Carry a government photo ID. Brewpubs can and do refuse service without it.

Licensing rules also change what brewpubs can do. In many states they can serve their own beer on site but cannot sell it to take away, so do not count on growler fills. Rules vary by state and change, so check what applies in your city.
Make it a tasting, not just a night out

A crawl is a rare chance to compare the same style from three breweries on one night. Pick one style, such as a wheat beer or a pale ale. Order it at every stop. Write three words for each: aroma, bitterness and finish. By the third brewpub you will have learned more about that style than a month of random pints would teach you.

The gap most people find is vocabulary. You can tell the beers are different but not say how. Training your nose and palate on reference samples turns "I liked the second one" into a note you can use.

Your first step: pick three brewpubs within a short cab ride of each other, check their closing times and decide in the group chat how everyone gets home.
faqs: How many brewpubs should a crawl include?
Three is plenty for a four hour evening. It leaves time to eat, taste properly and get home safely.
What is the drinking age for brewpubs in India?
It varies by state, from 18 in some states to 25 in others. Carry a government photo ID.
Can I take beer home from an Indian brewpub?
In many states brewpubs can only serve beer on site. Rules vary by state, so check locally before planning on growler fills.
